title: Christian Cousins, ‘Kindergarten Cop’ Child Star, Dies at 43
description: Christian Cousins, a child star who appeared in “Kindergarten Cop” alongside his twin brother Joey, has died after battling liver disease, his brot
body:
Christian Cousins, a child star who appeared in “Kindergarten Cop” alongside his twin brother Joey, has died after battling liver disease, his brother Jonas Roeser announced on Instagram on Oct. 22. He was 43.

	“RIP my dear brother Christian Cousins,” Roeser wrote. “It’s hard to share that my brother, Christian Cousins, has passed away. Christian and his twin brother, Joseph “Joey” Cousins, are my brothers through my biological father. They grew up in California while I was in Washington and I didn’t get to know them until I was in college. Before that, I grew up watching them on television in ‘Knots Landing’ and the lead role of Dominic in ‘Kindergarten Cop’ with Arnold Schwarzenegger. But those roles are only a small part of how I’ll remember Christian. He was a character, full of passion and energy, with big stories and even bigger dreams. Christian had been very sick with liver disease. It brings me comfort to believe he is now in heaven with his mother, free from the pain he was carrying. Rest easy, Christian. I hope your soul is at rest and that you’ve found peace. You are my brother and you will be missed.”
	


	Cousins played Dominic in the 1990 action comedy “Kindergarten Cop” starring Arnold Schwarzenegger.  He first made his young acting debut in the 1988 TV series “Highway to Heaven” and also appeared in “Roxanne: The Prize Pulitzer,” “Father Dowling Mysteries,” “Eerie, Indiana,” “Intruders,” “Empty Nest” and more. His film debut came in “Kindergarten Cop” and he then landed a role on the CBS soap opera “Knots Landing,” appearing in 57 episodes.

schema.headline: Christian Cousins, ‘Kindergarten Cop’ Child Star, Dies at 43

title: Box Office: Johnny Depp’s ‘Ebenezer’ Makes $1.5 Million in Previews
description: For the first time since 2018’s “Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald,” Johnny Depp is back on the big screen in a major Hollywood movie wit
body:
For the first time since 2018’s “Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald,” Johnny Depp is back on the big screen in a major Hollywood movie with Paramount’s “Ebenezer.” His new, darkly comedic take on “A Christmas Carol” has made $1.5 million in previews at the box office.

	“Ebenezer,” directed by Ti West, is expected to open with $20 million domestically and another $20 million overseas. Paramount spent $38 million to produce the spin on the classic Charles Dickens tale, plus another $50 million to market it, and it’ll need the adoration of Depp’s diehard fans to power it through the holiday season.
	

	Depp stepped back from Hollywood during his domestic abuse trial against his ex wife Amber Heard, but he was still making indie and international movies abroad. He stayed busy with the 2020 drama “Minamata,” the 2023 period piece “Jeanne du Barry,” and he directed the 2024 biopic “Modì, Three Days on the Wing of Madness.” “Ebenezer” marks his first major Hollywood film in eight years since “Fantastic Beats” (Warner Bros. replaced him with Mads Mikkelsen in the third film, “The Secrets of Dumbledore”). Up next, he’ll star in Lionsgate’s revenge thriller “Day Drinker” with Madelyn Cline and Penelope Cruz, set to hit theaters in March.

	The “Ebenezer” cast also includes Rupert Grint as Scrooge’s employee Bob Cratchit, Ian McKellen, Daisy Ridley, Sam Claflin, Andrew Riseborough as the Ghost of Christmas Past, Tramell Tillman as Christmas Present and Robert Strange as Christmas Yet to Come.

schema.headline: Box Office: Johnny Depp’s ‘Ebenezer’ Makes $1.5 Million in Previews

title: Jon Hamm, Andrew Koji to Star in Takashi Miike’s Tokyo-Set Psychological Thriller ‘Bullfrog’ as Mk2 Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Jon Hamm (“Mad Men,” “Your Friends & Neighbors”) and Andrew Koji (“Street Fighter,” “Warrior”) are set to star in “Bullfrog,” a psychological thril
body:
Jon Hamm (“Mad Men,” “Your Friends & Neighbors”) and Andrew Koji (“Street Fighter,” “Warrior”) are set to star in “Bullfrog,” a psychological thriller from cult Japanese filmmaker Takashi Miike (“13 Assassins”).

	Paris-based mk2 Films (“Minotaur”) has boarded international sales on “Bullfrog,” one of the hottest projects to hit the AFM. CAA Media Finance is handling North American sales and financing. 


	Set in a near-future Tokyo under lockdown, “Bullfrog” follows a Japanese detective (Koji) and a former FBI profiler (Hamm) as they track a mysterious serial killer in a dangerous cat-and-mouse game.
	

	The film is written by Eric Jordan Baker and produced by Nathan Ross (“Big Little Lies,” “Sharp Objects,” “Dallas Buyers Club”) and David Styne (“Love Means Zero”). Japanese production company OLM will oversee production in Japan, with Misako Saka also producing. Principal photography is planned for summer 2027.

	“Takashi Miike is one of the great provocateurs of contemporary cinema, and Bullfrog feels like a thrilling opportunity to see him at his most audacious,” said Fionnuala Jamison, managing director of mk2 Films. “Eric Jordan Baker has written a razor-sharp, wickedly dark thriller, and with Jon Hamm and Andrew Koji on board, we couldn’t be more excited to bring this extraordinary project to international audiences.”

	Miike joins a roster of internationally acclaimed auteurs represented by mk2 Films, whose recent slate has enjoyed a strong run on the festival circuit. At this year’s Cannes, the company presented Andrey Zvyagintsev’s “Minotaur” which won the Grand Prize and is now France’s Oscar candidate; as well as Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo’s “Ben’Imana” which picked up both the Caméra d’Or and FIPRESCI Prize; and Marine Atlan’s “La Gradiva” received the AMI Paris Grand Prize at Critics’ Week. MK2 Films is also behind Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor’s “NAZA” which won the Special Jury Prize at Venice.
	

	One of Japan’s most prolific filmmakers, Miike has directed more than 100 features and built an international cult following with his provocative approach to genre cinema. His films include “Audition,” “Ichi the Killer” and “13 Assassins,” as well as the Cannes competition titles “Hara-Kiri: Death of a Samurai” and “Shield of Straw.” His upcoming projects include “Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo” and the untitled Kyoto project.

	Hamm, who earned an Emmy and two Golden Globes for his portrayal of Don Draper in “Mad Men,” recently starred in “Your Friends & Neighbors” and appeared in “Top Gun: Maverick.” 

	Koji, whose credits include “Bullet Train,” “Boy Kills World,” “Snake Eyes” and Netflix’s “Black Doves,” will next appear in the fourth season of “Gangs of London.” He also stars in Legendary’s “Street Fighter.”

schema.headline: Jon Hamm, Andrew Koji to Star in Takashi Miike’s Tokyo-Set Psychological Thriller ‘Bullfrog’ as Mk2 Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Zohran Mamdani Launches Two-Day NYC Youth Video Game Design Competition With a Transit Twist Ahead of ‘GTA 6’ Launch (EXCLUSIVE)
description: This weekend, New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani will debut a youth video game design competition in the headquarter city of “Grand Theft Auto 6” d
body:
This weekend, New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani will debut a youth video game design competition in the headquarter city of “Grand Theft Auto 6” developer Rockstar Games just ahead of the much-hyped game’s Nov. 19 release.

	Launching Saturday, the NYC Game Jam is a two-day competition in which young New Yorkers design and build a video game around a set theme. 

	The inaugural inspiration for the competition is the theme “Get There Already,” a transit-based concept that is more family friendly than the M-rated “Grand Theft Auto” franchise. Per the Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment, “Participants will build a game about getting across the city. Every game must be about transit or the experience of getting around a city, suitable for all ages, and free of violence, weapons, and other illicit activity.”
	

	Three finalists will be chosen by a judging panel made up of industry veterans. Mamdani will announce the winning team on social media in days after the competition with first place set to receive $3,000, second place a $1,500 prize, and third place with a $500 prize, all to be shared among team members.

	The Office of the Mayor, the Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment (MOME) and the New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYCEDC) are sponsoring the NYC Game Jam competition which will be accompanied by a career fair to allow participants to meet with gaming studios that are hiring. These studios will showcase their games and work, discuss open positions and offer mentorship.

	According to MOME, New York City’s games sector supports about 7,900 jobs across approximately 380 firms and generates $2.6 billion in annual economic impact. About 65 percent of those firms are small or independent studios, though the most well-known NYC-based games employer is “GTA 6” maker Rockstar Games and its parent company Take-Two Interactive.
	

	The Game Jam is the latest program that the city has launched in support of the gaming industry with MOME previously investing a bachelor’s degree program in digital game design at CCNY, launching the Gaming Pathways Program to introduce high school students to game design careers, and establishing the Digital Games Industry Council to advise the City on policy. 

	Additionally, NYCEDC runs the Game Design Future Lab with NYU Tandon.

	“Whether you’re exploring the forests of Hyrule or riding across the frontier at Nuevo Paraíso, video games invite us into worlds born from the imagination of their designers. And that creativity represents an enormous opportunity here in New York City,” Mamdani said. “As the industry grows, we want to make sure the next generation of game developers and designers can build their futures right here at home. This Game Jam is a chance to open the door to that industry for young New Yorkers, connect them with the people shaping it and give them the tools and support to turn their biggest ideas into careers.”

	“Right now, New York City is having an undeniable moment as a global hub for digital games, with hundreds of independent studios and major industry leaders calling the five boroughs home,” NYC Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment commissioner Rafael Espinal. “Under Mayor Mamdani’s leadership we are seizing this momentum to open doors for our city’s youth. Events like the ‘Get There Already’ Game Jam bridge the gap between passion and profession, giving young New Yorkers hands-on experience and direct access to the studios shaping our $2.6 billion gaming industry.”

schema.headline: Zohran Mamdani Launches Two-Day NYC Youth Video Game Design Competition With a Transit Twist Ahead of ‘GTA 6’ Launch (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Billy Evans Says ‘You Can See Everything’ Made Him Look ‘Crazy’: ‘I Would’ve Preferred’ Not to Be the Villain, but ‘It’s Entertainment’
description: It seems Billy Evans has no hard feelings for “You Can See Everything” directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, even if their A24 documentary
body:
It seems Billy Evans has no hard feelings for “You Can See Everything” directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, even if their A24 documentary about Elizabeth Holmes portrays him as a villain.

	“I would preferred for that not to be the case, but it’s entertainment,” Evans told CBS. “I didn’t get to control the edit.”

	In a promo clip for a forthcoming “Sunday Morning” interview, correspondent Matt Gutman asked Evans, “Are you OK being the subject of entertainment at your expense, which makes you truly look like a conniving, manipulative villain?”
	

	Evans agreed that the film makes him look “crazy” but said, “My goal was to have people see Elizabeth. And when I watch that movie, I see the person that I love and exactly who she is.”

	In “You Can See Everything,” Evans spars with Fielder as the comedian attempts to investigate whether his romantic partner, the convicted fraudster behind the blood-testing company Theranos, is being honest. But while he inhabits an antagonistic role in the film, Evans previously said in a social media “AMA” that he does not regret agreeing to the documentary “at all” and had seen “almost all of” Fielder’s previous work before inviting him into his and Holmes’ San Diego home.

	Asked to pick one misconception about the film to dispel, Evans wrote on X, “That I somehow control Liz. Anyone who actually knows her would find that idea hilarious. She’s fiercely independent, strongwilled [sic], and my best friend. We are partners in every sense. We challenge each other, disagree, and face the world together. Her closest friends are also some of my closest friends. If I ever mistreated her, they’d have my head.”
	

	“You Can See Everything” is an experimental, three-hour documentary that captured the zeitgeist and the box office when it premiered in October. The movie reached $80 million after just four weekends, becoming the second-biggest doc ever in North America. The film is still rolling out internationally as awards season kicks into gear.

Billy Evans, the partner of imprisoned Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, told @CBSMATTGUTMAN that he loves “You Can See Everything” directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, despite their portrayal of him as “crazy” in the documentary film.“When I watch that movie, I see… pic.twitter.com/8i0ZoIhfab— CBS Sunday Morning 🌞 (@CBSSunday) November 13, 2026

title: Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan’s Heist Drama ’12 12 12′ Feels Like a Bad Video Game: TV Review
description: From “Ocean’s Eleven” to “The Italian Job” to Netflix’s “Money Heist,” robbery has long been a major subgenre in film and television, and now Apple
body:
From “Ocean’s Eleven” to “The Italian Job” to Netflix’s “Money Heist,” robbery has long been a major subgenre in film and television, and now Apple TV‘s “12 12 12” is delivering its own take. Created by Jim Keeble and Dudi Appleton, the high-voltage thriller follows disgraced FBI Agent Jack Strickland (Anthony Mackie), who, driven by rage and a desire for revenge, begins tracking known thief Paul Galvin (Jamie Dornan) across Europe after the biggest heist in the continent’s history. Instead of a straightforward narrative, “12 12 12” revolves around three stages of the heist: the 12 months Paul and his team spend planning the operation, the 12 hours it takes to execute their plot and the 12 days after the crime as Jack scrambles to bring them to heel. While the revolving timelines are certainly intriguing, the bloated cast, utterly confusing storylines and clumsy dialogue make for a painfully puzzling watch. ‘TK’
	

	“12 12 12” opens inside a vault at the Lindenhof Bank in Zurich, Switzerland, on Christmas Eve. In the haunting quiet, a lockbox door swings open, and Alberich (Julius Feldmeier), a contortionist, emerges fully nude, unfolding his limbs and snapping and cracking his bones and muscles back into place. It is time for the $1 billion burglary to begin. Elsewhere, the rest of Paul’s expansive crew jumps into action. As the reserved larcenist sits in church mass, speaking quietly with his hot-headed older brother Bobby (Jack Kesy), Paul’s father-in-law Serge (José Garcia) and a couple of other men stand in a train tunnel under the Lindenhof and begin drilling a hole into the vault. Meanwhile, Kira (Kali Reis), a train expert, creates a diversion for the Zurich police. In the Lindenhof security room, Gunda (Hildegard Schroedter) sets a trap for her coworker, then turns all the bank’s cameras toward the vault Alberich has just entered.
	

	Though audiences watch Paul’s masterplan get underway, this isn’t really where “12 12 12” begins. As Jack explains at the start of nearly every one of the eight-episode first season, “The FBI Principles of Crime says a high-asset robbery is 12 months in planning and 12 hours in execution. A bank robber who is not caught within 12 days is not caught at all.” Though viewers are introduced to the extensive cast in the first hour of the pillage, the series constantly shifts timelines, moving through the 12 months of planning, the 12 days after the heist and all 12 hours of the thieves attempting to steal the cash and make it out of Zurich undetected and unscathed.

	Keeble and Appleton certainly wanted to deliver their own take on heist dramas, but the execution leaves much to be desired. Countless characters and ever-changing timelines create a baffling, exhausting tale. Told chronologically, or even in reverse, the show could have been engrossing. Instead, the entire series runs out of steam by the second episode, as audiences struggle to grasp what’s happening and how the storylines and characters connect. Because the time frames feel so haphazard, there is little room for character connection or emotional grounding. Moreover, Jack’s desperate need for vengeance clouds his judgment, leading him to make maddening choices that endanger himself and Zurich police detective Lena (Sallie Harmsen), who tries to help him when no one else will. As a result, “12 12 12” feels like trying to simultaneously watch a multiplayer video game across multiple levels and points of view,

	This isn’t to say “12 12 12” doesn’t have truly stunning visuals, with locations including Marseille, France, the snowy Swiss Alps and even Milan, Italy. But the scenery, countless explosions, gun battles and fist fights do little to save a narrative buried under the weight of hijinks and confounding plot choices. The differing timelines do such a disservice to the show overall that when a huge twist is revealed toward the end of the season, it lands like a raindrop, and is a far cry from the jaw-dropping discovery it should be.

	Heists will always be a familiar trope for thrillers, and it makes sense that Keeble and Appleton wanted to put a unique spin on a tried-and-true genre. Unfortunately, cramming every idea, thought and character they could conceive into this world — creating eight overblown episodes — proves to be a massive misstep. In the end, the grand finale feels like a relief instead of a revelation.
	

	The first two episodes of “12 12 12” debut Nov. 13 on Apple TV, with the remaining episodes airing weekly on Fridays.

schema.headline: Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan’s Heist Drama ’12 12 12′ Feels Like a Bad Video Game: TV Review

title: Taylor Swift to Perform at CMAs for the First Time in 13 Years
description: Taylor Swift will perform on the CMA Awards Wednesday for the first time in 13 years, ABC and the Country Music Association announced Friday morni
body:
Taylor Swift will perform on the CMA Awards Wednesday for the first time in 13 years, ABC and the Country Music Association announced Friday morning.

	Swift had already publicly declared, upon getting a CMA nomination this year, that she would attend the show, but there was no indication until now on how or whether she intended on participating in the show beyond being an audience member. 

	No information was given about what Swift will perform on the show, although it’s a good bet it will consist partly or wholly of her nominated song, “I Knew it, I Knew You,” her contribution to the Disney/Pixar film “Toy Story 5.”

	Her previous appearance as a performer on the show came in 2013, when she received the Pinnacle Award and performed the song “Red” with Vince Gill and Alison Krauss. 

	Swift’s last time attending or appearing on the show at all was in 2016, when, as a surprise, she came on stage in the program’s last minutes to present the Entertainer of the Year award to Garth Brooks.



	

	



	This year marks the 20th anniversary of her first appearance at the CMA Awards, shortly after the release of her self-titled debut album. Her first win came in 2007, when she won the Horizon Award as the CMA’s choice for the best new artist. In 2009, she became the youngest artist ever to win the top prize at the awards, Entertainer of the Year.


	With the release of “1989” in 2015, Swift declared she was picking a lane between pop and country, and pop had won out, although she did not burn any bridges with the country community. 

	The release of “I Knew It, I Knew You” marked her first brand new song in more than a decade to be marketed as a country song — and to make it to No. 1 at country radio format — although she had dabbled in the genre in the intervening years with album tracks like “Betty” and a vault track duet with Chris Stapleton, “I Bet You Think About Me.”


	The show airs from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena on Wednesday from 8-11 p.m. ET/PT on ABC and Disney+, with next-day streaming availability on Hulu.

	Other performers already announced for the Lainey Wilson-hosted 60th annual CMA Awards include leading nominee Ella Langley, Cody Johnson, Miranda Lambert, Tim McGraw, Kacey Musgraves, The Red Clay Strays, Zach Top, Tucker Wetmore, Luke Combs, Vince Gill, Megan Moroney, Mumford & Sons, Chris Stapleton, Lainey Wilson and Stephen Wilson Jr. Additionally, Brothers Osborne, Luke Bryan, Halestorm, Hardy and Marcus King will take part in a tribute to Brooks & Dunn. A salute to Dolly Parton is also planned.
	

	Beyond her picking up a nomination for a CMA Award for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” the song — co-written by Jack Antonoff — is also being campaigned for an Oscar for best original song, and was submitted in the category of song of the year for the Grammy Awards.

schema.headline: Taylor Swift to Perform at CMAs for the First Time in 13 Years

title: The Best Grateful Dead Merch to Gift Deadheads in 2026
description: The Deadhead fandom lives on, if not in an intergenerational obsession with the iconic rock band than in ongoing collaborations and products that ce
body:
The Deadhead fandom lives on, if not in an intergenerational obsession with the iconic rock band than in ongoing collaborations and products that celebrate their legacy.

	For serious collectors, this year’s releases include a newly remastered 50th-anniversary edition of “Steal Your Face,” a four-LP pressing of the band’s legendary 1985 Merriweather Post Pavilion performance and an expansive 20-CD box set revisiting the group’s 1985 summer tour. There’s also “An American Beauty,” a new photography book chronicling three decades of the band’s history, and Upper Deck’s first-ever Grateful Dead trading card collection, complete with rare parallels and autographed collectibles.


	The band’s influence extends well beyond the record store, too. South Korean streetwear label thisisneverthat has released a new collection of Dancing Bears jackets, hoodies and knitwear, while designer Mira Mikati has put her colorful spin on the band’s instantly recognizable imagery. For something a little more unexpected, there are Grateful Dead-branded home goods, holiday ornaments and even a new streaming platform offering access to the band’s extensive archive of live performances.

	Below, check out some of the best Grateful Dead merch to gift the Deadheads in your life this year — just in time for the holidays.

		

						
			
	

	
					
		

										BESTSELLER						

					The Complete Annotated Grateful Dead Lyrics		

	
		For the Deadhead who treats liner notes like scripture, The Complete Annotated Grateful Dead Lyrics is the definitive text. Edited by David Dodd, the book gathers every officially released lyric and pairs it with rich annotations that unpack the band’s folk, blues and beat-poet influences. It’s a deep-dive companion for anyone looking to decode the mythology behind “Ripple,” “Dark Star,” and the rest of the Dead’s sprawling, psychedelic canon.	
		
	

		

						
			
	

	
					
		

										NEW RELEASE						

					An American Beauty: Grateful Dead 1965–1995		

	
		This large-format hardcover features 275 photographs by celebrated Dead photographers including Jay Blakesberg, Rosie McGee and others, documenting the band, its fans and its countercultural influence across three decades. 	
		
	

		

						
			
	

	
					
		

										new release						

					Grateful Dead – Merriweather 6/30/85 Live on Vinyl		

	
		The previously unreleased complete June 30, 1985, Merriweather Post Pavilion performance gets a four-LP edition. One of the clearest choices for a Deadhead with a serious vinyl collection.	
		
	

		

						
			
	

	
					
		

										NEW RELEASE						

					Mira Mikati ‘I Need a Miracle’ T-Shirt		

	
		The designer’s five-piece ready-to-wear capsule reimagines classic Dead imagery with colorful, hand-drawn illustrations and playful Dancing Bears graphics. A particularly strong fashion-forward addition that goes beyond the usual band tee.	
		
	

		

						
			
	

	
					
		

										limited-edition						

					Vineyard Vines x Grateful Dead 		

	
		This capsule takes the band’s psychedelic graphics into prep territory, combining Vineyard Vines’ signature whale with Dancing Bears motifs across shirts, sweatshirts, hats and ties. Good for someone who wants something more understated than traditional concert merchandise.	
		
	

		

	

	
					
		

										NEW RELEASE						

					Upper Deck Grateful Dead Trading Cards		

	
		Upper Deck’s first-ever Grateful Dead trading card collection is one of the most novel gifts this year. Each box includes the complete 50-card base set plus five additional cards, with possibilities including rare numbered parallels and cards signed by archivist David Lemieux.	
		
	

		

						
			
	

	
					
		

					The Music Never Stopped (Live) LP Box Set		

	
		One of the best Grateful Dead live albums, “The Music Never Stopped” contains songs recorded in concert over 25 years (from 1969-1994), packaged in this six-record vinyl box set.	
		
	

		

						
			
	

	
					
		

					Here Beside the Rising Tide: Jerry Garcia, the Grateful Dead, and an American Awakening		

	
		This sweeping 528-page chronicle by Jim Newton traces Garcia’s journey from a raw folk–bluegrass musician to the face of a generation, while mapping the band’s odyssey across festivals, political flashpoints and cultural revolutions.	
		
	

		

						
			
	

	
					
		

					Dancing Bears x Slowtide Fleece Blanket		

	
		Slowtide partnered with Grateful Dead drummer Mickey Hart for this summer capsule collection last year. The lineup consists of three quick-dry towels, donning  psychedelic graphics originally created on canvas with acrylic paint by Hart. “Slowtide towels offer a state of the art design that are both sand and water resistant. Paired with my images, these towels offer a unique take on what a beach towel of the future is,” Hart said in a statement.	
		
	

		

			
			
			
			
	

	
					
		

					Jammer Quick-Dry Kitchen Towel		

	
		Started by three friends, Slowtide creates comfort for outdoor hangouts. The brands whole vibe is basically creating various blankets and towels to keep your beach hangs both comfortable and stylish. You’ll spot their towels at trendy places including the Los Angeles, Portland and Palm Springs Ace Hotels. However, it’s their recent Grateful Dead collaboration that keeps selling out. This line includes over 12 different Grateful Dead-inspired blankets, towels and robes. Brighten up your kitchen with this adorable quick-drying towel, decorated with the band’s iconic Steal Your Face logo. 	
		
	

		

			
			
			
			
	

	
					
		

					Shashibo Shapeshifting Box		

	
		This Grateful Dead fidget toy is a magnetic puzzle cube that can be transformed into 70 unique shapes. But aside from serving as a relaxing way to keep your hands busy throughout the day, it also doubles as a charming decor piece to add to your office or living room. For the partnership with the iconic band, the cube is upgraded with famous Grateful Dead imagery such as colorful dancing bears and the famous “Steal Your Face” album art.	
		
	

		

			
			
			
			
	

	
					
		

					Grateful Dead x Chinatown Market Classic Crocs		

	
		The Grateful Dead gets the Croc treatment with this limited-edition tie-dye release currently available on StockX. 	
		
	

		

			
			
			
			
	

	
					
		

					Jerry Garcia Funko Pop		

	
		Jerry Garcia is the definition of cool even in Funko Pop form, which sees the famous rocker in his classic aviator sunnies and electric guitar. 	
		
	

		

			
			
			
			
	

	
					
		

					Steal Your Face Backpack		

	
		This special day backpack will make the perfect companion for everything from the hiking trail to the beach to an outdoor concert. Tagged with the legendary “Steal Your Face” album artwork, the limited edition backpack also features MaxCold insulation, padded straps, two divided compartments to keep items organized and even a built-in bottle opener.	
		
	


						
			
	

	
					

		

						
			
	

	
					
		

					Grateful Dead Tie-Dye Playing Cards		

	
		These make the best addition to any camping trip or long car ride. The full pack comes with different funky images, all featuring the band’s classic skull imagery and tie-dye patterns.	
		
	

		

			
			
			
			
	

	
					
		

					Dancing Bears Guitar Strap		

	
		If dad’s a true deadhead, it’s time for them to represent on their guitar while they slowly pick through the opening of “Uncle John’s Band.” If you’re looking for something a little less dancing bear, we love this Steal Your Face strap with the bands name printed across. And while you’re at it, pick up a few guitar picks as well. 	
		
	

		

			
			
			
			
	

	
					
		

					Grateful Dead Stickers		

	
		Let’s not even pretend for a second that you’re not into stickers. If you’ve made it this far in the “Best Grateful Dead Merchandise” list, you definitely have a steal your face sticker on something or another in your life. What’s a few more?

title: ‘Prima Facie’ Review: Cynthia Erivo Brings Conviction, but Not Necessarily a Conviction, to an Impassioned but Clunky Legal Drama
description: When a successful stage play is transferred to the screen, the typical concern is how much to “open it out” for the new medium: too little, and you
body:
When a successful stage play is transferred to the screen, the typical concern is how much to “open it out” for the new medium: too little, and you wonder why they bothered; too much, and you lose the electric intimacy that galvanized audiences in the first place. It’s to the credit of “Prima Facie,” director Susanna White’s earnestly impassioned film of Australian playwright Suzie Miller’s recent West End and Broadway hit, that anyone unacquainted with the material would hardly guess that it originated as a one-woman show. Set in the lofty, intricately hierarchical world of London law, it feels convincingly populated, with a clear, embedded sense of place; it moves at a decent clip, only giving into stagy speechifying in the final stretch.
	

	And the subject matter still grabs you by the collar: Reflecting on the shattering psychological impact of rape, and the long odds of bringing perpetrators to justice even from within the legal system, it lands in U.K. cinemas this week at a particularly timely moment — as the high-profile conviction of Russell Brand marks an all-too-rare victory for sexual assault survivors.

	It’s just a shame it isn’t a better movie. Miller’s adaptation of her own play runs hot and cold, as splitting the source’s theatrical stream-of-consciousness flow into dialogue and running interior monologue yields mixed rewards. There’s some awfully heavy-handed writing here, but elsewhere the script is intelligently conceived — the contrast between inner and outer voices defines the dual consciousness and everyday code-switching of protagonist Tessa Ensler, a working-class Black woman and Cambridge-educated barrister defying her lack of born privilege to swiftly rise through the ranks. And Cynthia Erivo, inheriting a virtuoso role that won Jodie Comer a Tony and an Olivier, does a creditable job with it — most powerfully in the film’s middle stretch, which offers a raw-nerved, pain-racked study of PTSD in the immediate aftermath of sexual assault.
	

	What scuppers proceedings, however, is White’s stiff, literal-minded direction, which too frequently cheapens the writing with aggressively on-the-nose imagery, while rhythmically and aesthetically, the filmmaking tends toward the flatly televisual. 

	Alarm bells sound as early as the opening shot, which tracks the glittery black sneakers on Tessa’s feet as she heads to court, the skittering hip-hop beat of Ciara and Missy Elliot’s track “Move” filling the soundtrack via her personal headphones. It’s an effective enough visual and aural cue that Tessa’s roots are far removed from this stuffy realm of white men and white wigs. It probably doesn’t need the accompanying cutaways to various dusty portraits of said men in said wigs on the walls, least of all when Tessa’s aforementioned inner monologue is already articulating that difference, identifying the silver-spoon elites who dominate her profession as “thoroughbreds.” And we certainly don’t need, in the midst of this speech, cutaways to images of actual thoroughbred horses; mere minutes in, “Prima Facie” betrays a strange lack of confidence in its own cinematic storytelling.

	Tessa may not be like the others — a pointed choice has been made not to conceal Erivo’s own elaborate piercings and many ornate tattoos, which extend onto her hands — but, as her opening voiceover somewhat redundantly underlines, “I’m here too.” And she’s getting noticed for all the right reasons: Her impressive performances at the Old Bailey have seen her surge past many of her current chambers peers in status and demand, while she’s being courted by a more prestigious practice. Her main reason to stay put is her posh, charming colleague Julian (Daniel Ings), with whom she has flirtatious chemistry that blooms, one evening, into after-hours office sex. “I want this,” Tessa says internally as they get down to business — subtlety is rarely the film’s strong point.

	Still, “Prima Facie” is keenly and commendably focused on the specific politics of consent in intercourse, observing the differing dynamics in three separate encounters between the same two people. In the second, after a boozy dinner date, Tessa takes Julian back to her place, and the sex is joyfully hot and heavy; in the third, mere hours later, he takes advantage of her queasy, semi-conscious state to force himself upon her. 
	

	It’s a scene exactly as discomfiting as it needs to be, played with unvarnished candor by both actors — and again overegged by White’s direction, with banal images of broken glass repeatedly inserted into the action, while doomily percussive scoring by Isobel Waller-Bridge threatens to take matters into “Law & Order: SVU” territory. None of these flourishes has as much impact as Erivo’s numb, hollowed-out physicality in the scenes following the rape — as Tessa reports Daniel to the police the very next morning, and faces an irrevocably changed future.

	From here, the film shifts into predominantly procedural mode. Tessa, who has defended the accused in many a sexual assault case before, suddenly finds the shoe on the other foot — all her favored legal tactics and loopholes now turned against her as she accepts the near-impossibility of proving her case in her own professional sphere. “Prima Facie” thus never seems likely to develop into a rousing courtroom drama, though its more interesting, bitterly ironic dramatic potential is also curtailed. Tessa’s arc stops short of a difficult moral reckoning with her chosen career, while latent domestic conflicts remain as such — in particular, her passive-aggressive relationship with her steadfast mother (an excellent Noma Dumezweni), a cleaner who fears her daughter will undo all her social self-elevation by going public with the case.

	Instead, the film’s big dramatic swing is an unconvincing swerve back to the play’s original format — as a despondent Tessa takes the stand to argue for systemic change on behalf of all survivors like her who have struggled to be heard in a court of law. It’s a showy, declamatory climax, delivered with poised fury by Erivo. But if the message is on point, the scene doesn’t quite ring true: It’s perhaps the moment when “Prima Facie” feels least engaged with the reality of all women in Tessa’s position, and most concerned with engineering a theatrical triumph for its indubitably impressive heroine. Even for one of Britain’s brightest young barristers, the only win here can be a rhetorical one.

schema.headline: ‘Prima Facie’ Review: Cynthia Erivo Brings Conviction, but Not Necessarily a Conviction, to an Impassioned but Clunky Legal Drama

title: Lena Dunham on Media’s Misogyny Over ‘Girls’: ‘People Were Angrier at Us for Giving Handjobs on TV Than They Were at Walter White or Tony Soprano’
description:
Lena Dunham and Allison Williams are still getting used to people actually liking “Girls.”

	“We are not used to the way people feel about the show
body:
Lena Dunham and Allison Williams are still getting used to people actually liking “Girls.”

	“We are not used to the way people feel about the show now,” Dunham said during a conversation with Allison Williams at New York City’s Swarovski store on Thursday evening. “It’s a daily surprise.”

	When “Girls” premiered in 2012, Dunham and her co-stars became frequent targets of criticism over everything from the show’s explicit sex scenes to its portrayal of privileged young women navigating their ’20s in New York City. 
	

	“I was saying that when the show came out, the way that people talked about our behavior — I was like, ‘People are angrier at us for just being girls who sometimes give hand jobs on TV than they are Walter White or Tony Soprano.'”

	Allison added: “I don’t know how many people in the room watched it in real time, but if you didn’t, I’ve got to tell you something: We are not used to the way people feel about the show now.”

Lena Dunham called Allison Williams about reviving “Girls” before she contacted HBO or anyone else:“It started with us and it ends with us! And I was nervous when I called you because she’s a busy mom and producer and iconic Scream Queen and she might not want to return.”… pic.twitter.com/H0wPt9n1IY— Variety (@Variety) November 13, 2026


	“There was a website called Gawker, which, fuck it forever,” Williams joked, referencing the now-defunct gossip blog notorious for its biting celebrity takedowns. “They referred to us as our dads’ daughters in the articles that covered the show. They didn’t even call us by our actual names.”

	Now, ahead of the “Girls” revival, Dunham says “People are understanding, and people like the idea that young women would be naughty and complicated and weird and self-aware. They recognize that you could potentially be a woman under 25 and have some modicum of self-awareness.”
	

	Dunham added that Williams was her first call — “before HBO, before anyone” — to ask about joining the revival. “It started with us and it ends with us!” 

	“And I was nervous when I called you because she’s a busy mom and producer and iconic Scream Queen and she might not want to return,” she added.

	As reported earlier this month, HBO prepares to revive “Girls” for five episodes, with production scheduled to begin in 2027. Dunham will reprise her role as Hannah Horvath alongside Williams, Jemima Kirke as Jessa Johansson, Zosia Mamet as Shoshanna Shapiro and Andrew Rannells as Elijah Krantz. Judd Apatow will also return as executive producer.

schema.headline: Lena Dunham on Media’s Misogyny Over ‘Girls’: ‘People Were Angrier at Us for Giving Handjobs on TV Than They Were at Walter White or Tony Soprano’

title: Microsoft Making Progress To Fully Restoring Outlook After Thousands of Memes Expressing Joy From Outage
description:
Microsoft
                          Logs Off, But Close to Restoring Outlook ...
body:
Microsoft
                          Logs Off, But Close to Restoring Outlook ...
                          Killing Workers' Dreams of Friday Without Emails
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 13, 2026
                            5:43 AM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Microsoft's huge headache restoring Outlook and other services that went down Thursday is now bleeding into Friday... but the company says it's making progress ... putting an end to the memes being created by employees estatic by not having emails.
      
    
            The tech company, headquartered in Redmond, Washington, saw its popular Microsoft 365 services, such as Exchange Online and other email services, come to a screeching halt around 1:30 pm ET Thursday for many users who first started reporting issues in the morning hours from Asia to the United States.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Twitter Tweet.
      
    
            Since then, the company has been doggedly attempting to solve the issues and get their servers back up and running ... but, so far, they've fallen short of fully restoring access. Company execs, however, say they are using “a measured approach to identify and repair affected infrastructure.”
      

            The problem is that about 130,000 users from the roughly 430 million people using the Microsoft 365 app have been impacted by the worldwide outage. Most of the impacted users are reporting issues with Microsoft Outlook.
      
    
            One thing's for sure ... the company says there is no evidence of a cyberattack or a data breach.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Twitter Tweet.
      
    
            But some good news came in overnight ... Microsoft reported on X that its seeing "encouraging recovery progress in Europe," and "North America is also improving."
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Twitter Tweet.
      
    
            The company put the blame for the outage on an "elevated load" on its servers, noting that other servers had become "unexpectedly unavailable."

                          Robert Pattinson Called In ...

James Bond Search
                          Robert Pattinson Called In ...
                          After James Lowden, Callum Turner Fail to Impress
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 13, 2026
                            7:10 AM PST
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  November 13, 2026
                                7:47 AM PST
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Robert Pattinson wasn't among the first actors to audition for James Bond ... but he could end up stealing the role right out from under them.
      
    
            According to Puck, there's a theory making the rounds that director Denis Villeneuve and the franchise's producers weren't sold on their initial 007 hopefuls ... prompting them to bring in bigger names like Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The original contenders included "Slow Horses" star Jack Lowden, Josh O'Connor and Callum Turner ... but Puck reports Pattinson and Hoult screen-tested after the others, fueling speculation the filmmakers weren't impressed enough to pull the trigger.
      

            And Pattinson may have a serious leg up on the competition ... with Puck reporting his deal was significantly sweeter than those offered to the other actors.
      
    
            While Lowden and O'Connor were required to commit to four Bond films if cast, Pattinson reportedly negotiated that down to three ... along with a much bigger payday.
      
    
            Even more telling ... the outlet reports Pattinson's deal was so difficult to negotiate that some involved in the process questioned why filmmakers would go through all that trouble unless they REALLY wanted him.
      
    
            Pattinson also has a connection to Villeneuve, having worked with the director on the upcoming "Dune: Part Three" ... and the filmmaker reportedly always wanted to see him audition.
      
    
                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            Of course, nothing's official just yet. The hunt to replace Daniel Craig is reportedly nearing its end ... with an announcement expected before Christmas.
      
    
            Sounds like Batman might be trading his cape for a tuxedo ...

title: Kansas Mom Who Plowed Truck Into Soccer Game Killing 2 Won't Be Charged
description:
Kansas Soccer Field Tragedy
                          Mom Who Killed 2 in Truck Crash Won't Be Ch
body:
Kansas Soccer Field Tragedy
                          Mom Who Killed 2 in Truck Crash Won't Be Charged
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 13, 2026
                            6:08 AM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            An unnamed Kansas mom who drove her truck into a soccer game, causing the deaths of two people -- including a 6-year-old child -- will not be charged in the fatal accident.
      
    
            After toxicology results didn't turn up any signs of intoxication, Sedgwick County District Attorney Marc Bennett told reporters ... "I have zero evidence that this was in any way impacted by intoxication, driving under the influence."
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Bennett added that not only did he find no evidence of an intentional crime, he found evidence proving there was no intentional crime.
      

            The driver had crashed her truck into the crowd at Wichita's Stryker Sports Complex on Oct. 17.
      
    
            We reported earlier ... witnesses of the event said that the driver didn't appear to be intoxicated and after the vehicle came to a stop, she apparently told the crowd she fell asleep and accidentally hit the gas.
      
    
            Wichita PD spokesperson Andrew Ford previously told us that the driver had been detained and questioned by police in a hours-long interview.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The victims in the fatal accident had previously been identified as 6-year-old Cole Adrian and 35-year-old Nicholas Schafer ... with 10 others -- including 5 children -- suffering injuries.
      
    
            After the accident, Cole's father, Chris Adrian, told the New York Times ... "Cole was an incredible kid and could put a smile on anyone’s face."

title: NBA Star Chris Bosh Linked to Palisades Fire Case by Arson Suspect's Defense
description:
Palisades Fire
                          What's Chris Bosh Got to Do with It?!
body:
Palisades Fire
                          What's Chris Bosh Got to Do with It?!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 12, 2026
                            6:06 PM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Jonathan Rinderknecht lawyer is trying to prove he didn't start 2025's deadly Palisades fire ... and is pointing a finger at Chris Bosh's mansion instead.
      
    
            According to court documents obtained by the California Post, Rinderknecht's lawyer wants to introduce testimony from retired Cal Fire investigator Michael T. Cole about a possible firework launched from the NBA star's house.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The filing said ... "Mr. Cole is expected to testify that during his 2025 investigation of the Palisades Fire he observed and documented a mark and an associated burn and smoke trail on the driveway and rear patio area of the residence at (redacted), and that, based on his training and experience, those marks are physical evidence of a launched firework."
      

            The former Miami Heat star was reportedly renting out the house when the fires started, according to The Post.
      
    
            Prosecutors slammed the request in their own filing, saying Cole has "zero qualifications, training, or experience."
      
    
            They said ... "His entire 'expert' opinion is based on six drone photographs of a brown stain on the driveway taken in either February 2025 or 2026. No up-close in-person inspection, no other testing. Six drone photographs, that’s it."
      
    
            Rinderknecht's defense for the re-trial argues that fireworks possibly caused the devastating blaze ... not him.
      
    
            As you know, Rinderknecht is accused of sparking the blaze by using his lighter to set vegetation on fire. He's denying the allegations.
